assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube opened neutrino astronomy: a cubic-kilometre Cherenkov detector in Antarctic ice that established a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos well above atmospheric backgrounds and later associated a flare with the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane. A new observational window built on a detector concept, which is the kind of achievement I weigh most heavily.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led the IceCube project and its AMANDA precursor; Spiering was a founding figure of the Baikal and IceCube efforts and of the broader neutrino-telescope programme. The two-name credit is a workable configuration, though a very large collaboration and other pioneers (for example in AMANDA and Baikal) mean the allocation is not trivial.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation of the diffuse flux has come from several analyses and channels, and ANTARES and KM3NeT/Baikal-GVD provide partial cross-checks. The source-identification picture (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068) is still developing but the core discovery is stable, so recognition now is timely rather than premature.
uncertainties: Individual sources are still few and the origin of most of the diffuse flux is unresolved.
Credit among the founding figures of the neutrino-telescope programme could be contested.
I rely on my own general knowledge of the field and have not verified details independently here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and have redefined what is measurable, including gravitational redshift at the millimetre scale. They underpin a likely redefinition of the second and test fundamental constants and dark-matter models.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and made the first demonstrations; Ye's group drove the accuracy and stability to the current record levels, including strontium clocks and the optical frequency comb link. Hall and Hänsch were already recognised in 2005 for combs and Wineland in 2012 for ion clocks, so a Katori-Ye pairing is a clean and natural allocation.
assessment.maturity: Many independent labs (JILA, RIKEN, NIST, PTB, SYRTE and others) have reproduced and compared lattice clocks, with international clock comparisons. The technology is mature, extensively confirmed and stable, and the work is well aligned with the metrology tradition of the prize.
uncertainties: Credit for related precursors, such as Ye's collaborators or other lattice-clock groups, may be argued.
Some of the sharpest applications, including a redefinition of the second, are still pending.
Atomic physics is outside my own expertise and I would defer to colleagues on the finer attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Event Horizon Telescope delivered the first images of black-hole shadows (M87* in 2019, Sgr A* in 2022), a direct strong-field test of general relativity on horizon scales. It combines a global mm-VLBI array, extreme calibration and imaging methods, which I respect as instrument and systematics work.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed using the shadow as a probe, Doeleman led the EHT array and observing campaign, and Zensus led the European VLBI and the Max Planck contribution. The collaboration has about 300 members, so any three-person selection is a hard allocation and several others would have a legitimate claim.
assessment.maturity: The images are independently consistent across the 2017 to 2018 epochs and several imaging pipelines, and the Sgr A* result supports the picture, but the polarisation and time-variability interpretations are still evolving. The discovery itself is solid, but the committee may still see it as early.
uncertainties: The collaboration-scale credit problem is severe and the three credited names may not match what the committee considers decisive.
Imaging-pipeline dependence and model-dependent mass and spin constraints remain open.
The role of theorists and modellers in the interpretation may be argued.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The BeppoSAX discovery of X-ray afterglows and the subsequent optical and radio counterparts settled the long-standing debate about gamma-ray burst distances, placing them at cosmological distances and linking them to massive stars and compact mergers. It was an instrument-led breakthrough with lasting consequences for time-domain astronomy.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX wide-field and narrow-field X-ray detections that provided arcminute positions; Kulkarni's group led the optical, radio and redshift follow-up that fixed the cosmological distance. This is a natural split of the decisive contributions between the X-ray localisation and the redshift confirmation, though others (for example in the optical identification) would also have claims.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed thoroughly over 25 years by Swift, HETE-2, Fermi and gravitational-wave associations such as GW170817. The interpretation is stable, so the discovery is fully mature, if somewhat late given the generation of discoverers.
uncertainties: Attribution is contested among the X-ray, optical and radio teams (including van Paradijs and others who are not on this list).
Because the credited names are fixed to the supplied strings, I cannot propose some people who may be central.
The prize may be judged to be more astronomy than physics by some colleagues.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP produced the first full-sky, high-precision map of CMB anisotropies and fixed the cosmological parameters to percent-level precision, establishing the concordance LambdaCDM model with the age, matter content and reionisation epoch. It was a landmark in instrument design, with differential radiometers and exquisite control of systematics.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission and the instrument team, Page led much of the instrument and design work and Spergel led the cosmological parameter analysis. This reflects the instrument, mission and interpretation roles well, but the 2006 and 2019 prizes already recognised COBE and cosmology theory, which complicates the case, and Planck's follow-up overlaps.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed by Planck, ACT and SPT, which agree with WMAP within errors. The result is mature, but a significant part of its impact has been overtaken by Planck, so the prize may be seen as retrospective.
uncertainties: Overlap with the COBE prize (2006) and Planck may weaken the novelty argument.
Large WMAP team means the three-name configuration may omit decisive contributors.
Current Hubble-tension debates do not change the data but could shift emphasis.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, from the superfluid to Mott insulator transition to fermionic Hubbard simulations and quantum gas microscopes, has opened a platform where many-body models are realised and measured with single-site control. It is an experimental platform whose impact on many-body physics and quantum technology is clearly lasting.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch) proposed the Bose-Hubbard realisation, Greiner and Bloch demonstrated the Mott transition, and Esslinger brought fermionic Hubbard and transport. Bloch, Zoller and Esslinger form a defensible trio, but Greiner, Cirac and others are strong alternatives, and the credited set is not unique.
assessment.maturity: Repeated by many groups worldwide, and the platform is mature and increasingly quantitatively benchmarked against theory. Recognition would be timely, though overlapping with the 2012 and 2025 prizes in quantum control and macroscopic quantum phenomena.
uncertainties: The allocation among Bloch, Greiner, Esslinger, Zoller and Cirac is genuinely ambiguous.
Recent quantum-technology prizes may reduce the room for a further quantum-optics award.
Condensed matter and quantum simulation are outside my own expertise, so I would rely on the colleagues on this point.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Silicon microstrip and hybrid pixel detectors transformed tracking at colliders, enabled vertex detection for heavy-flavour physics and were essential to the Higgs discovery, and the pixel technology spread to X-ray imaging and medicine. For me this is the clearest example of detector work as a driver of discoveries, in the tradition of Charpak's prize.
assessment.attribution: Heijne contributed the early silicon detector and readout concepts at CERN, Parker developed the microstrip and later 3D detectors, and Campbell led the Medipix and hybrid pixel readout development. The three roles are distinct and complementary, but other pioneers (for example in microstrip, such as Kemmer and Hyams, and in pixel work such as Heijne's collaborators) may be argued.
assessment.maturity: The technology is extremely mature and used in every major collider experiment and many imaging applications, so confirmation is not in doubt. The main timing question is whether the committee regards instrumentation as a recognised discovery class today.
uncertainties: Disputed historical priority between several groups for silicon strip detectors.
Attribution is very diffuse, because a large number of people contributed to the technology.
The committee may favour discoveries over instruments in a given year.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Trapping and cooling antihydrogen and precision tests of CPT and the antiproton and proton magnetic moments are direct probes of fundamental symmetry, now down to parts per trillion or better. This is close to my own field of antimatter measurements, and I can judge the experimental difficulty of such work.
assessment.attribution: Gabrielse led the trapping and antiproton and positron cooling work (ATRAP) and the electron g-2 measurement, Hangst led ALPHA, which achieved antihydrogen trapping and spectroscopy, and Ulmer led the BASE antiproton measurements. The credit among ATRAP, ALPHA and BASE is a genuine allocation problem, but the three-name set is coherent.
assessment.maturity: Results are consistent with CPT so far and several key measurements, such as the 1S-2S line and the antiproton magnetic moment, have been reproduced or improved. The programme is still progressing, so the case is solid but the maturity is somewhat earlier than for the others.
uncertainties: No violation of CPT has been observed, so the case rests on technique and precision rather than a discovery of new physics.
The ordering of ATRAP and ALPHA credit is contested.
Some of the most compelling results (gravity on antihydrogen) are very recent.
